title.narrative: Strengthening prosecutorial methodology to investigate and dismantle organised criminal networks in Colombia (SPMOC)

description.narrative: This project will strengthen the Prosecutor’s Office capacity to dismantle organised criminal networks by developing, validating, and beginning institutional adoption of a unified methodology to investigate and prosecute these structures as integrated criminal systems. The project will deliver: (1) a methodological and operational framework that sets principles, structured prosecutorial processes, analytical criteria, and practical tools; and (2) a specialised module for illicit economies linked to fuel-station networks, including typologies, risk indicators, territorial and financial linkages, and evidentiary routes. Activities include a diagnostic based on case analysis and practitioner consultations, a co-design workshop with territorial and central teams, iterative drafting and refinement of both components, and pilot use in selected units supported by case-based exercises. These activities will produce operational guidance and a practical adoption roadmap that supports internal uptake beyond the project period. This system-focused approach improves strategic case design, strengthens analytical-investigative coordination, and enhances the State's ability to weaken criminal structures over time. UK support ensures methodological rigor, continuity with previous engagement, and independent quality assurance through strategic oversight, technical review, and financial support. At the same time, this methodological approach is aimed at reducing crime by enabling prosecutors to map and dismantle entire criminal networks rather than isolated nodes, preventing their regeneration.
